title: GetPt: Graph-enhanced General Table Pre-training with Alternate Attention Network

problem.claim: Complex table structures and layouts are difficult to support in general tabular data understanding.

gap.claim: Most existing works target specific table types and neglect tables with complex layouts.

contributions.claim: GetPt is a unified pre-training architecture for general table representation, including tables with complex structures and layouts.
The architecture converts tables into heterogeneous graphs with multiple edge types and applies a transformer to jointly model table semantics and structure.
The Alternate Attention Network models contextual information across token, cell, and table granularities, supported by three pre-training objectives and pre-training on a large table dataset.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report fine-tuning and evaluating GetPt on table type classification and table structure recognition.
The authors report that GetPt outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods on the evaluated tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Tables are important information carriers, and tabular data understanding has motivated large-scale pre-training research.
Existing methods commonly focus on specific table types and leave complex-layout tables insufficiently supported.
GetPt represents tables as heterogeneous graphs and jointly models their semantics and structure with a specialized transformer.
An Alternate Attention Network captures context across tokens, cells, and tables, while multiple pre-training objectives support downstream tasks.
The model is evaluated on table type classification and table structure recognition, with reported improvements over existing state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: The model uses attention across tokens, cells, and tables.

interpretation.claim: Modeling multiple granularities may help connect local content with higher-level structure.

application.claim: When designing representations for hierarchical data, evaluate whether interactions across granularities should be modeled explicitly.

exception.claim: The abstract does not isolate the effect of the Alternate Attention Network from the other components.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset names, sizes, or pre-training details.
The abstract does not provide evaluation metrics, numerical results, or baseline details.
The abstract does not report ablations or component-level comparisons.
